newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm vs dollar, market unmatched.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm vs dollar, market unmatched.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was firm against the dollar on Tuesday in an unmatched market, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.49 against the dollar compared to 53.57 on Monday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at 87.45 from 88.
"It's not that the supply is so much to warrant an appreciation of the shilling, it's just that there is no demand absolutely," a dealer from a leading bank told Reuters.
"The fact is many banks are long in dollars but there is no demand," another dealer said.
Dealers said they expected a further appreciation of the shilling against the dollar with inflows from Tuesday's coffee export auction due today.
"Many banks are positioned for a further appreciation," another dealer added.
The money market was liquid with overnight rates quoted between 8-10 percent from 10-15 on Monday.
